title: Data on Ultra-high Net Worth Individuals and Their Families Who Have Been Granted Singapore Citizenship
what_it_is: Data on Ultra-high Net Worth Individuals and Their Families Who Have Been Granted Singapore Citizenship

sections.label: Citizenship for ultra-high net worth individuals
sections.summary: MP asks about ultra-high net worth individuals granted Singapore Citizenship since 2000; MHA says a researcher's 3,500 figure was misleading and he was misquoted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs for each year since 2000 (a) what is the number of ultra-high net worth individuals and their families, with a net worth of at least US$50 million, who have been granted Singapore Citizenship; (b) of which, how many of them obtained Singapore Citizenship after having set up a family office in Singapore; and (c) how many obtained Singapore Citizenship through other avenues.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: That is not a primary criterion for assessment for Singapore Citizenship.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: There were recent media reports that said that a researcher based in South Africa had estimated that 3,500 high-net-worth individuals were due to get Singapore Citizenship in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) issued a statement on 25 April 2023 stating that the reports were highly misleading and had no credible basis.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: We do not know how the researcher had arrived at these figures and the grant of Singapore Citizenship for the rest of 2023 has not been decided yet.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: After our statement was issued, the researcher wrote to MHA to say that he had been misquoted by the media.

sections.label: Singapore Citizenship assessment factors
sections.summary: MHA says high net worth does not guarantee citizenship; applications are assessed on contribution, jobs, skills, family ties, integration and commitment to sink roots.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: As mentioned in MHA's statement on 25 April 2023, having high net worth does not guarantee Singapore Citizenship.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Each Singapore Citizenship application is assessed on a broad range of factors, which include the ability to contribute to Singapore, the number of jobs that the applicant or his business may be able to create in Singapore, the special skillset and/or education that the applicant may possess, the applicant's family ties to Singaporeans, the ability to integrate and the commitment to sink roots in Singapore.

sections.label: MHA rebuttal and misquote
sections.summary: MHA issued a statement rebutting the report, and the person supposedly quoted wrote to say those things.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: What we do know and what is factual, is that we issued a statement categorically rebutting the report, and the person who was supposedly quoted has written to us to say all these things.
